definition: 1Password is a password manager that stores sign-in details and other secrets in encrypted vaults.
example: A project team shares a service login through a restricted vault rather than sending the password in chat.

definition: A 360 campaign coordinates a marketing message across multiple channels and audience touchpoints.
example: A museum launch uses matching themes in email, street posters, social video, and on-site signage.

definition: 3D modeling software creates and edits digital objects defined in three spatial dimensions.
example: A designer builds a chair model and checks how its proportions look from several angles.

definition: Solid and surface modeling represent three-dimensional geometry as volumes or as bounding surfaces, respectively.
example: An engineer shapes a curved housing with surfaces and converts the closed form into a solid to check wall thickness.

definition: 3DMark is a suite of standardized benchmarks for evaluating graphics and gaming performance.
example: A reviewer compares two graphics cards with the same 3DMark test and settings.

definition: Four-dimensional construction modeling links elements of a 3D project model to the construction schedule.
example: A planner plays back the model to check whether a hoist is installed before façade work begins.

definition: TCID50 is a measure of infectivity defined by the dose estimated to produce detectable infection in half of the tissue culture test units.
example: A reader distinguishes a published TCID50 result from a count of physical particles.

sense_note: The label names a JavaScript renderer but does not identify the product or meaning of ABC clearly enough to distinguish a specific tool.

definition: Academic English is the register used to read, discuss, and present arguments and evidence in educational or scholarly contexts.
example: A student qualifies a research conclusion and cites the evidence that supports it.

definition: Academic record-keeping maintains authoritative records of students’ enrollment, coursework, and progress.
example: A registrar reconciles course completions before issuing a transcript.

definition: An accelerated failure time model relates predictors to multiplicative changes in the time until an event.
example: A researcher compares how two treatments stretch or shorten the modeled time to relapse.

definition: Accelerated Mobile Pages is a web framework that uses constrained markup and optimized resource loading to build fast-loading pages.
example: A publisher builds an AMP version of a news article using the framework’s supported components.

definition: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy is a behavioral psychotherapy that develops psychological flexibility through acceptance, awareness, and action guided by personal values.
example: A therapist helps a client identify a valued activity to resume even when uncomfortable thoughts are present.

definition: Accessioning formally receives and registers an item so its identity and custody can be tracked.
example: A museum gives an incoming object a unique identifier and records its provenance.
sense_note: The core recordkeeping sense is shared by collections and laboratory specimen workflows.

definition: The Accountancy and Passenger Ticket Issuing System, or APTIS, was a computerized rail ticketing system that linked ticket sales to accounting records.
example: A railway clerk issues a passenger ticket while the system records the transaction for reconciliation.

definition: The accounting cycle is the recurring sequence of recording transactions, preparing statements, and closing accounts for a reporting period.
example: An accountant posts year-end adjustments before preparing financial statements and closing revenue accounts.

definition: Accounting software records financial transactions and produces ledger, reconciliation, or reporting outputs.
example: A small business reconciles its bank statement against transactions recorded in the software.

definition: Accounts receivable management tracks what customers owe and follows invoices through collection or other resolution.
example: A credit controller uses an aging report to prioritize overdue invoices for follow-up.

definition: ACID Pro is a digital audio workstation designed for arranging loop-based music and editing multitrack recordings.
example: A producer combines rhythmic loops with a newly recorded vocal track.

definition: ACL Analytics is software for examining datasets and automating audit and control tests.
example: An auditor searches a payment ledger for duplicate payments and retains the resulting exceptions for review.

definition: Activated sludge is a wastewater treatment process in which a suspended microbial community removes organic matter before solids are separated from the water.
example: A treatment plant uses an activated sludge stage before releasing its clarified effluent.

definition: Active-HDL is a design and simulation environment for digital circuits described in hardware description languages.
example: An FPGA engineer simulates a counter design against a testbench before synthesis.

definition: ActivePivot is an in-memory analytical database for aggregating and exploring large datasets interactively.
example: A risk analyst changes portfolio groupings and recomputes exposure totals in a dashboard.

definition: ActivePython is ActiveState’s distribution of the Python language and runtime.
example: A maintenance team uses the specified ActivePython environment to run an existing automation script.

definition: Acunetix is a web application security scanner that helps identify potential weaknesses in authorized web properties.
example: A security team reviews scan findings and assigns defensive remediation tasks.

definition: AD Model Builder is a framework that uses automatic differentiation to fit complex statistical models by numerical optimization.
example: A fisheries scientist fits a population model and evaluates uncertainty in its fitted parameters.

definition: AdaBoost is an ensemble method that trains successive weak learners while increasing emphasis on examples earlier learners misclassified.
example: A classifier combines multiple shallow decision trees to reduce mistakes on difficult observations.

definition: Adaptive equipment modifies how a person performs an activity to accommodate a functional limitation.
example: A person with limited grip uses an enlarged utensil handle to eat independently.

definition: Adaptive Insights is business planning software for budgeting, forecasting, and comparing financial scenarios.
example: A finance team models how a hiring delay changes next quarter’s spending forecast.

definition: Adaptive leadership mobilizes people to learn and change their practices when a problem cannot be resolved with existing expertise alone.
example: A department manager facilitates small experiments when new workflows have no established best practice.

definition: The ADDIE model organizes instructional design around analysis, design, development, implementation, and evaluation.
example: A training team identifies learner needs before designing lessons and later measures whether the lessons met their objectives.

definition: Additive manufacturing builds physical objects by adding material in layers or other successive portions from a digital design.
example: A prototyping shop prints a housing whose internal channels would be difficult to machine.

definition: Adjudication is a formal process for examining evidence and applying rules to decide a dispute or claim.
example: A hearing officer reviews the parties’ submissions and issues a reasoned decision.

definition: Administering blood tests involves carrying out the collection or point-of-care steps needed for an ordered blood analysis.
example: A qualified clinician verifies patient identity and documents that an ordered specimen was obtained.

definition: Adobe Analytics is a platform for measuring and analyzing digital customer behavior across visits and channels.
example: An analyst compares where visitors leave two versions of an online checkout.

definition: Adobe ColdFusion is an application server for building web applications in CFML and related technologies.
example: A developer uses ColdFusion to render a portal page populated from a database.

definition: Adobe Experience Platform Launch is a tag-management system for deploying and governing scripts and data collection rules across digital properties.
example: A measurement team updates an approved analytics rule without editing each page individually.

definition: Adobe Fonts provides a catalog of typefaces for use in supported design and web workflows.
example: A designer selects a typeface from Adobe Fonts and applies it consistently across a brand project.

definition: Adobe PhotoDeluxe was a consumer image editor for retouching pictures and making simple photo projects.
example: A user crops a scanned photograph and arranges it in a greeting-card layout.

definition: Adobe Substance 3D Designer creates procedural textures and materials through editable node graphs.
example: A material artist builds a stone surface whose crack density can be adjusted without repainting the texture.
